hook: SCP-8066 opens on a page about SCP-2006, the shapeshifter that loves to scare people, which has suddenly lost its powers and is frightened for the first time. The real file belongs to Dr. Randall Owings, head of Site-118's Department of Phobology, who appears to be the only person able to notice what is going wrong around him. It is a slow-build horror piece that ends in explicit body horror and torture, and it is part of the SCP Anthology 2024.
whyItMatters:
The article builds on an existing object. Knowing 2006's original premise, summarized in the archived description, a creature that wants to cause fear but only understands it through old monster movies, helps a great deal, because the story asks what happens when that limitation is removed.

It also borrows the antimemetic investigation format, where one immune researcher documents something nobody else can perceive, and then pulls the rug out from under that format.
thingsToNotice:
The structure is three pages: the 2006 file, Owings' 8066 log, and a final 2006 page. The log degrades on purpose, from formal incident reports to first-person notes, as SCP-106 is found curled up and whimpering, a dispatcher knows Owings' name, colleagues' faces drift, the exits vanish, and he cuts his arm to find nothing inside. Owings guesses at antimemes and memes, but the real clue is his question about how 2006 ever learned to call him Randy.

The ending answers it. The thing at his door says it is the old skin 2006 shed when it grew too big for a body, and drags him through the floor. The last page reclassifies 2006 as a law of nature and puts everyone in a box of their own fear: Price hollowed out by eyeless coworkers, Lowe crushed in a narrowing labyrinth, 106 forced to be happy in a white room, Japers' fingers cut off as guests eat his names, and Owings in a room of meat with needles driven through his eyes so he can see every box at once.

related.note: The shapeshifter whose sudden change opens this article.
Its containment cell is one of the first places where things go wrong.
